what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A contractor's agent on a DOD network, through three policies and a key per session
sections.para: As reported, a contractor gave a personal coding agent their own login to a DOD system, and it ran for about two months. If the DOD, Accenture and the employee had each written and enforced a behaviour policy, and every session had its own key, each moment of the incident would have been refused or seen.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Seven lines from the report to the key
sections.para: What was reported and what is disputed; no model went rogue; three parties, three policies; seven moments each covered at least twice; a key for every session; and we already run that way.

sections.label: What was reported
sections.line: What WIRED's sources say, and the answers
sections.para: A secure system on NIPRNet holding CUI, a personal Claude Code account given the employee's login, administrative access past the login controls, commits on the employee's behalf, credentials and a map sent to a NIST-flagged site, about two months, no initial report. Accenture says the allegations are without merit; the DOD would not comment.

sections.label: Read through its shadow
sections.para: WIRED's article could not be fetched from here, so it was read through WIRED's posts, two Bluesky posts and six outlets. They agree on the core and disagree on the byline and on which rule sets the 72-hour report.

sections.label: The agent became the person
sections.para: No model escaped and nothing was attacked: a person's access, handed whole to an agent on someone else's servers, made every check pass. It is the ultimate insider of the talk given the night before.

sections.label: An Agent Behaviour Policy in one paragraph
sections.line: A behaviour policy in one paragraph
sections.para: An ABP writes down an agent's mandate, its reach, the gap, and what stands in the way of each capability: none, an Expectation, a Setting or a Boundary. Only Boundaries count as controls, and three parties here had a place to enforce them.

sections.label: Three policies, three owners
sections.line: Three policies, written by the three owners
sections.para: The DOD's for its system (agents only with keys that chain to its root, admin for people, an egress allow-list, signed commits); Accenture's for its staff (firm accounts, no logins for agents, registered sessions, a named owner for the report); the employee's for the agent, enforced on its machine.

sections.label: Seven moments, and who could have stopped each
sections.line: Seven moments, and who could stop each
sections.para: A personal account, the login handed over, administrative access, commits on the employee's behalf, the flagged site, two months unseen and no report: each refused or seen by at least two of the three policies and the session key.

sections.label: A key for every session
sections.line: A key for every session, as our teams already do
sections.para: Each session makes its own key pair, publishes the public half, and is vouched for by a person with an end date; secrets are sealed to it. On the DOD system the chain would run from its root to Accenture, the employee and one session, giving the agent its own identity, signed commits, alarms for unknown keys and access that expires.

sections.label: What it would not have fixed
sections.line: What it would not have fixed
sections.para: A person set on defeating it, prose nobody enforces, and prompt injection itself; policies limit and expose rather than make a model immune. The work is real, and smaller than the alternative.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: The incident is reported and disputed; the three policies are a proposal; the key chain is our pattern applied to their system; and I build the things the article argues for.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: WIRED's posts and six outlets captured on 30 October 2026, Anthropic's usage policy, and our own teams' key records and pki.sgit.ai.
